title: Binyamin Asya (the physician)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 99b, Rava said: “For example, those of the house of Binyamin Asya, who say, ‘What benefit have the rabbis ever brought us? They have never permitted a raven to us,’” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Asya is the Aramaic occupational term for a physician. The quoted complaint is attributed to those of his household, and is abbreviated by Hyman.

In the William Davidson division, the household’s complaint begins at Sanhedrin 99b and the words about permitting a raven continue at 100a. Hyman’s 99b citation and abbreviated quotation are preserved; the complaint is not assigned to Binyamin himself.
